subject: ArrTags v1.2 plan (Phases 15-21): the accepted-for-planning scope docs/planning/v1.2.md and the proposed decisions ADR-022..ADR-028, decision gates DG-15..DG-22

findings.description: ADR-022 claims successive runs cover a scope larger than QueueCapacity by advancing a cursor past the 'covered prefix'. But IWorkHintSink.TryEnqueue returns a single bool that LibraryWorkQueue sets false for THREE different cases: key already in flight, key already pending (coalesce), and pending count >= Capacity (overflow). The ADR's own Context acknowledges this ambiguity but the Decision never resolves it. The service cannot tell a covered (coalesced/in-flight) item from an overflow-dropped item, so it cannot know where the covered prefix ends. A naive 'advance by the number of TryEnqueue==true results' under-counts coalesced items (already-covered), causing the same prefix to be re-covered every run (the F4 bug persists); a naive 'stop at the first false' stalls on a coalesced duplicate. As written, the whole-scope coverage guarantee required by the plan's acceptance criterion ('cover the whole scope over time (round-robin)') is not established.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-022.md Context ('The TryEnqueue boundary returns a boolean that does not distinguish a coalesce rejection from an overflow rejection') and Decision clause 1
src/ArrTags/Updates/LibraryWorkQueue.cs:153-171 (in-flight, pending-coalesce, and capacity-overflow all return false)
findings.recommended_action: Before acceptance, decide and record the enqueue-result vocabulary (accepted / coalesced / in-flight / overflow) and the exact cursor-advance rule (advance to the last contiguous covered item; stop at the first overflow; do not stop on coalesce). Either extend IWorkHintSink with a tri-state result or define a bounded rule that provably covers without needing the distinction (for example, stop the run at the first overflow).

findings.description: ADR-022 stores an 'opaque ordering position', but the only enumerator contract is IMediaLibraryEnumerator.EnumerateCandidates(int startIndex, int maxItems), which is an integer offset into a Jellyfin query ordered solely by ItemSortBy.SortName ascending. SortName is not unique (duplicate episode/movie names) and library content mutates between runs (scans add/remove/re-sort items). ADR-022 only resets the cursor on an enabled-library/item-type scope change, not on item insertion/removal. An integer offset therefore can silently skip or re-cover items whenever the library changes before the cursor, so the 'eventually cover the whole scope' guarantee is not sound. The ADR does not define how the position stays stable.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-022.md Decision clause 1 and clause 2 ('opaque ordering position') and clause 3 (reset only on scope change)
src/ArrTags/Media/JellyfinMediaLibraryEnumerator.cs:52-62 (OrderBy SortName only; no unique tie-break; query re-run per page)
findings.recommended_action: Define a stable cursor identity (for example a (SortName, itemId) seek key, or an opaque position that the enumerator can resume from) and add the enumerator capability it needs, or explicitly bound the guarantee (e.g., 'coverage is guaranteed only for a stable library and is best-effort under concurrent library mutation'). Also decide whether item add/remove should reset or advance the cursor.

findings.description: ADR-023 clause 1 says 'the worker re-enqueues exactly one fresh LibraryWorkItem ... for the same WorkItemKey'. LibraryWorkQueue.TryEnqueue returns false when the key is already in flight (per-item in-flight bound is exactly 1). LibraryWorkWorker calls CompleteProcessing(item.Key) only in the finally block AFTER ProcessWithRetryAsync returns. A re-enqueue issued from inside the processing/discard path (the natural implementation) is therefore coalesced away by the queue's own in-flight check, silently reintroducing F6. The ADR must specify that the re-enqueue happens after the in-flight slot is released.
findings.recommended_action: Add an explicit ordering clause: the worker records that the item discarded as a stale basis, releases the in-flight slot (CompleteProcessing), and only then enqueues the fresh current-version item; if the queue is stopped or full the re-enqueue is dropped (bounded). Require a coverage test that fails if the re-enqueue is issued before the slot is released.

findings.description: The stale-basis version discard and every other discard (item missing, ineligible, connection changed, configuration changed mid-processing) are all returned as WorkProcessingResult.Completed(reason) - a successful, non-retryable result whose only distinction is a free-text reason string. WorkProcessingResult has no version-mismatch code and the worker only sees IsSuccess/Retryability/Reason. ADR-023 does not define how the worker identifies 'a version-mismatch discard' as opposed to any other discard or a genuine success whose basis merely became stale afterwards. Comparing item.ConfigurationVersion to the current version in the worker would re-enqueue on successful-but-stale work too, which is broader than the ADR states. The ADR needs a bounded, machine-readable discard classification (or an explicit, bounded worker-side version comparison rule) before it is implementable as written.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Updates/ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor.cs:80-87 (second version guard also returns the success result)
findings.recommended_action: Define a bounded machine-readable classification on the processing result (for example a DiscardReason enum with ConfigurationStale/ItemMissing/Ineligible/ConnectionChanged) and state exactly which classification triggers the single re-enqueue. Add a test that a non-version discard does not re-enqueue.

findings.description: ADR-024 clause 1 keys the restore/removal on 'the render pass-through reason is NoDisplayableValue'. But RenderPassThroughReason.NoDisplayableValue is emitted for TWO different conditions in the renderer: (a) BadgeDefinitionResolver returned an empty selection (the intended F7 case), and (b) BadgeLayoutEngine.Build returned layout.IsEmpty for a NON-empty selection (nothing fits the safe area at the scaled geometry, e.g. a very large ExtraLarge size or a small poster). Implementing ADR-024 literally on the reason would therefore restore or REMOVE an ArrTags image when a valid displayable value simply could not fit, contradicting clause 1's 'empty resolved selection', clause 3 (other pass-through reasons preserve), and ADR-009's shorten/omit contract. This directly interacts with ADR-027's factor 2.0, which makes layout-empty more reachable.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-024.md Decision clauses 1 and 3 and Context ('resolve no displayable value ... empty selection')
src/ArrTags/Rendering/BadgeLayoutEngine.cs:109-130,240-243 (layout can be empty for a non-empty selection)
docs/planning/v1.2.md Goal F7 acceptance criteria ('An owned session that resolves an empty selection restores...')
findings.recommended_action: Discriminate on the resolved selection being empty, not on the NoDisplayableValue reason. Either add a distinct pass-through reason for layout-empty, or carry the resolved-selection-empty fact on the generation result and key the restore on that. Add a coverage test that a non-empty selection which cannot fit performs no mutation.

findings.area: ADR-028 (G6/DG-15): MB/KB unit-selection rule and min round-trip
findings.description: ADR-028 clause 1 (and the plan's G6 acceptance criteria) display byte limits 'of at least 1 MiB' in binary MB and WebhookMaxPayloadBytes in binary KB, with exact display/store round-trip at minimum/default/maximum. Three fields have a minimum below 1 MiB: ProviderResponseLimitBytes (min 64 KiB), SourceArtifactLimitBytes (min 64 KiB), DerivedArtifactLimitBytes (min 64 KiB). The rule does not say whether the unit is chosen per-current-value or per-field-range, how a range that straddles 1 MiB is labelled 'in the same unit', whether MB input is fractional, or how the integer <input type=number> round-trips 64 KiB (0.0625 MB) exactly. A naive integer-MB implementation fails the required minimum round-trip; a value-based unit switch makes the range-label unit ambiguous. The ADR must define the mapping before task 16.1 can satisfy the acceptance criteria.
findings.recommended_action: Specify the unit-selection rule per field (not per value), the allowed input precision/step, and the exact conversion algorithm (for example parse as a scaled integer in the chosen unit and round to the nearest byte) so that minimum/default/maximum round-trip exactly for ProviderResponseLimitBytes, SourceArtifactLimitBytes, and DerivedArtifactLimitBytes. State explicitly how the range label is expressed when the range spans the unit boundary.

findings.area: ADR-022 (F4/DG-19): cursor storage authority and torn-record reset
findings.description: ADR-022 clause 2 uses the existing StateRepository envelope but does not state the StateAuthority. This matters: StateRepository.Read treats an invalid Cache record as Discarded (deleted, caller sees a miss) but quarantines an invalid authoritative record. Clause 3 requires a torn cursor to 'reset to the start', which only happens naturally under Cache authority. The ADR should fix the authority (the cursor is non-authoritative and reconstructible) and the record kind, and should state the bounded scope-identity representation used to detect a scope change.
findings.recommended_action: State the cursor's StateAuthority (Cache, non-authoritative), the fixed record kind/id, and the bounded scope-identity tuple (enabled library-id set + supported item types) whose change resets it.

findings.area: ADR-022 / plan F4: which triggers use the cursor
findings.description: ADR-022 clause 4 says only scheduled/manual/post-scan use the cursor and that the bounded post-save trigger does NOT read or write it. The plan's F4 decision says 'whole-scope triggers only', and its acceptance criterion lists only event/webhook/per-item triggers as unaffected, omitting post-save. Since the post-save trigger runs the same LibraryReconciliationService enumeration from index 0, the plan and ADR disagree on whether post-save participates. This must be reconciled so the implementation branch on LibraryReconciliationSource is unambiguous.
evidence: docs/planning/v1.2.md Goal F4 decision and acceptance criteria
findings.recommended_action: State consistently whether PostSave participates; if it is excluded, say why (it is a user-triggered bounded prefix re-cover, not the scheduled/post-scan whole-scope guarantee) and add PostSave to the plan's unaffected-trigger list.

findings.area: ADR-023 (F6/DG-20): bound storage and clause-2 eligibility claim
findings.description: ADR-023 clause 2 bounds the re-enqueue to 'one per (item, connection, image surface, configuration version)' but does not say where that bound lives (the version-blind queue key cannot hold it; there is no per-key version set). It also claims an ineligible or no-longer-present item does not re-enqueue, but the version-mismatch discard fires BEFORE the item resolve/eligibility checks, so at that point eligibility is unknown; a re-enqueue can occur and the item is then discarded for the real reason on the next pass. That is bounded but is not what clause 2 states.
findings.recommended_action: Define the bound's storage/lifetime (for example the re-enqueued item carries the current version and the version check makes a same-version repeat impossible, so the bound is implicit), and restate clause 2 accurately: an item that is ineligible/absent is re-enqueued once and then discarded without further re-enqueue.

findings.area: ADR-024 (F7/DG-21): restore entry point and location
findings.description: ADR-024 says the coordinator 'drives the existing guarded lifecycle/restoration path' and lists ArtworkLifecycleCoordinator, but the pass-through to be changed occurs in ArtworkGenerationCoordinator, and the only restore entry point is ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync (internal), which requires an ArtworkLifecycleFence and only accepts a state whose State is Published. ArtworkLifecycleCoordinator has no single-subject restore API. The ADR should name the entry point and the fence it passes (Normal is permitted by ArtworkOperationFencing.AllowsNewRestoration), so task 20.1 does not invent a second path or bypass the per-subject gate.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-024.md Decision clauses 1 and 2 and References
src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:510-591 (internal RestoreAsync; requires Published; takes a fence)
src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkReconciler.cs:68,181 and ArtworkRecoveryDecisions (Normal-fence restoration resumes on restart)
findings.recommended_action: Name the exact call (for example a new internal coordinator/publisher entry that calls ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync under the current durable fence and the existing suite of subject gate/recovery), and confirm a Normal-fence restoration is intended and recoverable.

findings.description: ADR-026's status and Context state that it amends ADR-020 clause 4, 'which currently excludes paths from log output'. ADR-020 clause 4 as accepted contains no path exclusion: it excludes API key, webhook secret, SecretLease value, secret headers, raw bodies, full provider payloads, and mutable PluginConfiguration, and it allows 'bounded reason codes' plus item/record identifiers. The ADR therefore misdescribes the clause it is amending; the real change is to extend the allowed redacted-value set with a bounded log subject and to ADD a directory/path exclusion (which the ADR already asserts as 'still never logged'). "Still" is an overclaim.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-020.md Decision clause 4 (lines 48-54: no path item)
findings.recommended_action: Rewrite the amendment framing: clause 4 does not forbid a path but also does not name a file-name subject; this ADR adds the bounded log subject to the allowed set and adds the explicit directory/full-path exclusion. Update the amendment note wording accordingly.

findings.description: ADR-026 clause 3 names only the update work worker and the lifecycle removal event as explicit item-id fallback sites, and the plan's acceptance criterion repeats that pair. But MetadataReconciliationProcessor.Discard takes only itemId and is called from places where no usable MediaIdentity/path exists yet (version mismatch, item not present, identity creation failed, ineligible) as well as from places where an identity exists (read failure, changed basis). The ADR/plan should enumerate the mixed site and state that the discard helper falls back to the item id when no path is available, so implementation does not either drop the file name where it is available or attempt to thread a path where none exists.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:105-137,157-184,200-236,333-345 (Discard helper takes only itemId; identity may or may not exist)
findings.recommended_action: List every item-id-emitting site and its available subject (identity present or fallback), including the MetadataReconciliationProcessor discards, and require the log-subject helper to fall back to the item id when the path is absent.

findings.area: ADR-028 (G8/DG-17): mixed capture vs per-operation classification
findings.description: ADR-028 clause 2 defines a binary rule: restart-required only when the consumer captures the value at singleton construction, per-operation when the consumer resolves it from the current snapshot each operation. Several limits have BOTH consumers, so the rule is ambiguous: SourceArtifactLimitBytes is captured by ArtworkSourceReader/JellyfinArtworkImageAccess/SourceArtifactStore and also read per-operation by RenderLimitGuard via request.Limits; DerivedArtifactLimitBytes is captured by ArtworkPublisher and read per-operation by RenderLimitGuard/SkiaBadgeRenderer; MaxImageDimensionPixels is captured by ArtworkSourceReader and read per-operation by RenderLimitGuard. The ADR's 'only when' wording does not say how a mixed setting is classified or labelled.
findings.recommended_action: Define the classification for a mixed setting (recommended: restart-required if ANY consumer captures, with the note text stating that some paths apply immediately), and require task 16.2's set to record the per-consumer evidence for the mixed limits.

findings.description: ADR-028's Context enumerates the construction-captured examples as 'the artifact-size/decode limits' and 'the StateRepository-backed render cache TTL/quota and terminal-provenance retention'. It omits ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes (captured by SourceArtifactStore from StateRepository.Limits) and does not say that ProviderResponseLimitBytes, WebhookMaxPayloadBytes, and InventoryCacheMaxBytes are per-operation. README and data-model 3.12 also list only a subset. Task 16.2 must produce the complete set; the ADR should not present an incomplete example as the authoritative classification.
findings.recommended_action: Mark the Context list as illustrative and make task 16.2 the single owner that records the complete per-setting classification with consumer evidence, including ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes, the per-operation provider/webhook/inventory limits, and the mixed limits.

findings.description: The plan's per-phase documentation checklist (section 7) omits normative docs that enumerate the values being changed and will become stale: Phase 18 changes BadgeSize but lists only docs/data-model/03-06-badgedefinition.md, not docs/data-model/03-08-renderresult.md (lines 56-63) or docs/data-model/03-12-configuration.md (line 12, lines 96-101), both of which enumerate Small/Medium/Large. Phase 17 adds the F3 endpoint but does not list docs/architecture/12-performance-and-operational-limits.md, whose lines 126-130 are the F3 open-limitation paragraph ADR-025 says it amends. Task 21.2 provides a safety net, but the per-phase checklist should name them.
findings.recommended_action: Add docs/data-model/03-08-renderresult.md and docs/data-model/03-12-configuration.md to the Phase 18 checklist and docs/architecture/12-performance-and-operational-limits.md to the Phase 17 checklist.

findings.description: Two small points: (a) ADR-025 says the counter set covers 'at least' the listed counters while the plan's acceptance criterion requires a 'fixed bounded shape' - reword to make clear the listed set is the fixed minimum and additions require a decision; (b) the panel is served from the anonymous static page resource (ADR-016 clause 6) while its data endpoint is elevation-gated; the ADR should state the panel renders no data when the endpoint is not authorized (fail-closed, no error surface). Neither affects the soundness of the direction.
findings.recommended_action: Tighten the 'at least' wording to a fixed bounded shape and state the anonymous-page/elevation-gated-data split and its no-data fail-closed behavior.

findings.area: ADR-028 (G6/DG-15): 'sub-MB' description of the webhook field
findings.description: ADR-028 clause 1 calls WebhookMaxPayloadBytes the 'sub-MB' field; its validation range is 4 KiB-4 MiB (OperationalLimits.cs:186), so it is not inherently sub-MB. The KB display mapping is fine; the description should be 'the webhook payload limit field' rather than a size claim.
findings.recommended_action: Reword to identify the field by name, not by a value claim.

findings.description: ADR-023's status says it 'amends ADR-004's coalescing behavior'. ADR-004 records foundation operational limits and defaults; it does not define coalescing identity. The version-blind coalescing contract lives in docs/architecture/08-reconciliation-and-update-flow.md and the implementation. Retarget the status/references so the historical decision being amended is named accurately.
findings.recommended_action: Reference ADR-004 for the queue bound and architecture section 8 for the coalescing contract; describe the change as amending section 8's coalescing clause (plus the ADR-004 queue behavior it depends on).

findings.description: ADR-024 and the plan require the owned empty-selection case to 'remove the ArrTags image when the baseline was absent'. The badge pipeline cannot render without a source, so a Published state with an absent baseline is not produced by the normal coordinator path (the coordinator returns NoSource before the publisher). The removal branch is guarded and correct, but the plan's acceptance criterion for it may only be reachable via a synthetic state/publisher-direct test. Confirm the intended test vehicle or simplify the criterion.
findings.recommended_action: State how the absent-baseline removal case is exercised (synthetic persisted state or direct publisher test) or narrow the criterion.

findings.description: The ADR-027 decision is consistent with the code: both RendererConfigurationFingerprint and RenderFingerprint append the size only when it is not Medium, and BadgeSize numeric values are explicit, so adding ExtraLarge=3 changes no existing output; no RenderVersion or schema advance is required. Safe-area guarantees hold via the scaled-inset clamp in BadgeGeometry.ComputeEffectiveScale plus the layout engine's shorten/omit; at factor 2.0 a small poster can still yield layout-empty (existing behavior, see AR-V12-05). Task 18.1 must add the badge factor to the SizeFactor switch, which currently throws for unknown values.
findings.recommended_action: No change required to the direction; the implementation task must extend BadgeGeometry.SizeFactor and RendererConfiguration.Validate coverage for the new value.

findings.area: ADR-025 (F3/DG-18): no conflict with the v1.1 deferred status endpoint
findings.description: The v1.1 architecture review rejected a plugin-owned status endpoint only as a mechanism for an inline configuration-rejection message and stated 'no plugin-owned status endpoint is added in v1.1'. ADR-025 adds a read-only diagnostics endpoint for a different purpose, decided in the accepted v1.2 plan, and keeps the configuration save path unchanged; ADR-016 clauses 3/4 forbid a custom SAVE route, not a read-only elevation-gated read route. The plan correctly assigns the endpoint security review to security-reviewer (task 17.4) and the release security review to 21.5. No conflict.
findings.recommended_action: Record in ADR-025 that it is a distinct, v1.2 read-only surface and not a reopening of the v1.1 inline-rejection decision.

findings.area: ADR-026 (G9/DG-22): sites that need no change
findings.description: Of the call sites named in the review question, ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader, WebhookIntakeService, WebhookAuthenticationFilter, and LibraryReconciliationService emit no item identifier (connection id / counts / fixed reasons only), so they are not missed subject sites. The item-id sites are ArtworkGenerationCoordinator, MetadataReconciliationProcessor (including Discard - see AR-V12-12), the Sonarr/Radarr LogMatch sites, LibraryWorkWorker (key only), and ArrTagsLifecycleService (removal event).
findings.recommended_action: No change; use the enumerated site list in AR-V12-12 to make the plan's site coverage explicit.

findings.area: cross-cutting: decision gates and phase dependency
findings.description: DG-19, DG-20, and DG-21 are genuine mechanism choices proposed by ADR-022/023/024 and require explicit user acceptance; the plan and PLANS.md correctly state they must be accepted before the dependent Phase 19/20 implementation tasks are selected. DG-15/16/18/22 are recorded as user-resolved; DG-17 is split into a resolved note-text half and a jellyfin-expert spike. The phase ordering in PLANS.md matches the plan's dependency order, and the task-outline-to-phase mapping (V1.2-2..V1.2-8 -> Phases 15-21) leaves no outline task unowned. No missing owner for a deliverable or acceptance criterion was found. The plan is coherent as a plan; the F4/F6/F7/F8 and G6/G8 proposals need the changes above before acceptance.
evidence: PLANS.md Phases 15-21 and Decision Gates table
findings.recommended_action: No change required; keep the gates explicit and do not select Phase 19/20 implementation tasks until the ADRs are accepted after the changes above.

findings.description: The plan excludes F5 from v1.2 and keeps it Open; docs/limitations/00-index.md and open.md list F5 as Open, and README treats it as a known shipped limitation. The plan's exclusion is consistent with the register. (The review brief's 'F5 accepted' characterization does not match the register, which marks it Open, not Accepted; this is a wording nuance, not a v1.2 issue.)
findings.recommended_action: No action for v1.2; optionally align the F5 label with README's 'known shipped limitation' framing.

findings.area: ADR-028 (G8/DG-17): modal API unverified and correctly deferred
findings.description: The jellyfin-web modal/notification API is not pinned by the server repository (research section 9.2 notes the client contract is not pinned). ADR-028 clause 4 and task 16.4 correctly defer the modal mechanism to a jellyfin-expert spike with the note text as the fail-open behavior; the plan's live verification includes the note text. This is the right treatment of an unverified API and no architecture change is implied.
findings.recommended_action: No change; ensure the spike records the API's availability/stability per DG-17.

adr_directions.ADR-022: Direction (a persisted bounded cursor) is sound in principle, but the mechanism is underspecified: the enqueue-result ambiguity (AR-V12-01) and the cursor-position stability under the SortName-ordered integer-index enumerator (AR-V12-02) mean the whole-scope coverage guarantee is not established. Needs changes before acceptance.
adr_directions.ADR-023: Direction (re-enqueue at the stale-basis discard, keep the version-blind key and single-flight) is sound, but the decision omits the re-enqueue ordering vs the queue's in-flight check (AR-V12-03) and a machine-readable discard classification (AR-V12-04), so the fix as written can be coalesced away or over-trigger. Needs changes before acceptance.
adr_directions.ADR-024: Direction (owned empty selection is a restore obligation) is sound and consistent with ADR-002/ADR-003 (Normal-fence restoration is already permitted) and ADR-009 (explicit supersession for that case only). The reason-enum discriminator is defective (AR-V12-05) and the entry point is unnamed (AR-V12-10). Needs changes before acceptance.
adr_directions.ADR-025: Direction is sound and consistent with ADR-016 and the confirmed Jellyfin 12 plugin-controller/elevation contracts; the counter set is bounded and secret-free and the security review is correctly assigned. Only wording/checklist refinements (AR-V12-16, AR-V12-15). Sound to accept after minor edits.
adr_directions.ADR-026: Direction (bounded file-name subject with item-id fallback, directory never logged, security review) is sound and consistent with the redaction contract, and PrimaryPath is populated so the file name is available. The amendment framing misdescribes ADR-020 clause 4 (AR-V12-11) and the fallback-site list is incomplete (AR-V12-12). Needs changes before acceptance.
adr_directions.ADR-027: Sound as written: the fingerprint/version rules already include a non-default size and treat the default as identity-neutral, so ExtraLarge=3 needs no RenderVersion/schema advance and existing goldens stay byte-identical; safe-area guarantees hold. Sound to accept; only the plan's doc checklist needs the two data-model files added (AR-V12-15).
adr_directions.ADR-028: Direction (binary MB/KB display with bytes persisted, restart-required note text, modal fail-open) is sound, but the unit-selection/precision rule for ranges that straddle 1 MiB (AR-V12-06) and the classification of mixed-capture limits (AR-V12-13/14) are unresolved. Needs changes before acceptance.

recommendation: CHANGES_REQUIRED. The v1.2 plan is coherent as a plan: the goals, phase ordering, task-outline mapping, decision gates, and documentation checklist have no missing owner, and the release/security reviews are assigned. ADR-025, ADR-026 (modulo wording), and ADR-027 are architecturally sound directions; ADR-022, ADR-023, ADR-024, and ADR-028 are the right directions but are under-specified in ways that would either fail their own acceptance criteria or change behavior beyond what they state. Do not accept ADR-022/023/024/028 as-is. Specifically: fix ADR-022's enqueue-result/cursor-advance rule and cursor-position stability; add ADR-023's post-single-flight re-enqueue ordering and a machine-readable discard classification; make ADR-024 discriminate on the resolved selection being empty (not the NoDisplayableValue reason) and name the restore entry point; define ADR-028's per-field unit/precision mapping and the mixed capture/per-operation classification. These are resolvable from the repository; they are not user decisions. DG-19/DG-20/DG-21 remain genuine user acceptance gates and must stay gated before Phase 19/20 implementation tasks are selected.
summary: Reviewed the accepted-for-planning v1.2 scope and ADR-022..ADR-028 against the normative ADRs, architecture/data-model docs, limitations register, Jellyfin 12 research, and the installed code. Six HIGH findings: (1) ADR-022's coverage guarantee is not established because LibraryWorkQueue.TryEnqueue conflates coalesce/in-flight/overflow and the cursor-advance rule is undefined; (2) ADR-022's 'opaque position' is not stable because the only enumerator is an integer index over non-unique SortName and the library mutates; (3) ADR-023's re-enqueue must occur after CompleteProcessing or it is coalesced away; (4) ADR-023 lacks a machine-readable version-discard classification; (5) ADR-024 keys restore on NoDisplayableValue, which the renderer also emits for a non-empty selection that merely fails layout; (6) ADR-028's 'at least 1 MiB' unit rule and integer MB input cannot round-trip the 64 KiB minima exactly as required. Several MEDIUM findings: ADR-022 cursor authority/trigger consistency, ADR-023 bound storage, ADR-024 entry point, ADR-026's misdescribed clause-4 amendment and incomplete fallback-site list, ADR-028's mixed-capture classification and incomplete example set, and plan documentation-checklist gaps. ADR-025, ADR-026's direction, and ADR-027 are sound; ADR-027 is confirmed consistent with the fingerprint/version rules and safe-area handling. No BLOCKER: the direction set is the right one, the gates are correctly gated, and no conflict with immutable history was found. Status: CHANGES_REQUIRED.
